stem: Which of the following best describes a serious adverse event following immunisation (AEFI) according to WHO criteria?

options.text: Any reaction that causes the patient to miss more than two days of school or work
A reaction that results in a persistent or significant disability
A local injection site nodule that lasts for more than one week
A low-grade temperature of 38°C following a flu shot
A mild rash that settles without treatment

explanation: Serious AEFI includes outcomes such as death, life-threatening illness, hospitalisation, persistent or significant disability, or congenital anomaly.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because missing school or work is not a WHO criterion for a serious AEFI
optionExplanations.B: Correct because WHO classifies an AEFI as serious if it results in persistent or significant disability
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a local injection site nodule is usually a common local reaction, not a serious AEFI by itself
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a low-grade fever is a common minor post-immunisation reaction
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a mild self-limiting rash is not a serious AEFI unless it causes one of the WHO serious outcomes

source.hint: Recall the criteria involving the severity of medical outcomes, such as hospitalization or long-term impairment.
